items.title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
items.summary:
Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me.

But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.

GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff.

Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point.

I've been calling this low-speed mode . At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode.

items.title: GTA 5's Steam concurrents have gone up rather than down now that GTA 6 is out, suggesting a lot of PC players are waiting
items.summary:
Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over.

You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

(Image credit: SteamDB) GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" said GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

items.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
items.summary:
Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive.

Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. 

At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. Should you give the statue to him?

Give the statue to Halifax : He'll give you a watch to hold onto as collateral while he appraises the statue. Then he'll vanish for a while, trying to duck you, and you'll have to call him repeatedly to track him down again. Don't give the statue to Halifax : This is really just delaying the rest of the mission. You can keep the statue for now, but if you want to progress the mission you'll have to go all the way back to Capri at some point and give it to him anyway. So, you might as well just give it to him. Things shake out the same way no matter what you choose, but not giving it to him just means the mission will ultimately take longer to complete.

items.title: In the GTA 6 Delights robbery mission, help or don't help Frankie and Mario?
items.summary:
You'll face a choice in Chapter 2 of GTA 6 , when you're ready to help Vicky rob her boss, Frankie, at the Delights strip club in Port Gellhorn. Frankie asks you an important question and you've only got a couple seconds to respond:

"Can you dance? Yes or no, dude?" Frankie has caught you (as Jason) coming in the back door of the club as you and Lucia prepare to rob it. It's ladies night and one of the male strippers is out of commission, but Mario, the lead stripper, gets an idea when he meets Jason. Frankie has the same idea, and asks if Jason knows how to dance.

Yes, they are asking Jason if he can fill in as a male stripper for the show.

Help : If you help, Jason becomes a male stripper for the night, and yeah, it's hilarious. You dance, you strip, you grind on ladies in the crowd (including Lucia) while wearing a teeny tiny white thong, and it's just a whole lot of silly fun. And you still get to rob the place! Don't help : If you don't help, Mario walks away and the strip show is cancelled. But Frankie tries, by himself, to get the ladies worked up, performing a cringe-worthy (but funny) show on stage. Jason quickly interrupts it by putting a bullet into the ceiling and announcing that it's a robbery. You still get to rob the place. Personally, both versions are worth seeing, but Jason playing a stripper, and Lucia's utter delight at seeing him play a stripper, is way more fun.

items.title: Fact check: Does GTA 6 stop players from shooting inside gay nightclubs and crashing planes into buildings?
items.summary:
As players explore Leonida for the first time, misleading claims about Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun circulating on social media as evidence that Rockstar has toned down the series' violence. The two claims I've seen most often are along the lines of:

"GTA 6 prevents players from shooting inside of a gay nightclub" "GTA 6 makes planes bounce off of buildings to avoid 9/11 references" Both of these claims are misleading half-truths.

Does GTA 6 prevent players from shooting inside of a gay nightclub? ⛔ No, because there is no gay or LGBTQ nightclub in GTA 6. 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) It is true that you cannot use firearms inside of GTA 6 clubs, such as Nine1nine and The Vault . Grand Theft Auto 5 had the same restriction. But none of the clubs in GTA 6 are specifically presented as gay or LGBTQ clubs.

It is reasonable to speculate that Rockstar would want to avoid in-game scenarios that closely resemble the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting in Florida—the state Leonida parodies—but the studio has not stated as much.

Do GTA 6 planes just bounce off of buildings? ⛔ No, unless you've turned on a setting which reduces vehicle damage. 

Clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 airplanes smacking into tall buildings without taking any apparent damage have been used on social media to claim that Rockstar is intentionally preventing players from replicating 9/11-like crashes, or that the vehicle physics are shoddy.

The clips of ultra-strong planes aren't fake, but are achieved by turning on "Reduced Vehicle Damage" in the gameplay settings.

items.title: Valve may raise Steam Machine prices yet again: 'Memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels'
items.summary:
Valve has good news and bad news for anyone interested in buying a Steam Machine. All current reservations for the 512GB model have been fulfilled and there's stock remaining, so if you want one you can just head over to the purchase page and buy it—but the 2TB model is in shorter supply so signups for the waitlist are no longer being taken. And, sorry to say, there's also worse news: Valve says it won't be able to produce them in the quantities it had planned, and sounds like the price will be going up.

Despite their high prices, demand for Steam Machines was high enough that Valve implemented a randomized lottery system to buy one: Prospective purchasers signed up for a shot, a randomized selection were put in a reservation queue with a Steam Machine reserved in their name, and everyone else went to the waiting list to be notified when more reservation spots came open.

Valve said in July that it expected to have the reservation queue caught up by the end of 2026 , and that's now the case with the 512GB model: They're in an "an add-to-cart status," meaning that while supplies last, you can purchase one and it will be shipped straight away.

The situation is less happy for people waiting for the 2TB model, though. In an update posted today, Valve said all reservation holders have been sent their invitations to purchase but there are still people on the waiting list; those people won't lose their positions, but no one else will be allowed to join. 

It sounds like that situation is likely to hold for at least a few months, as Valve said it expects to have more information…

items.title: Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect
items.summary:
Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2."

I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff.

There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse. 

That is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's important to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box.

Gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions.

items.title: If you bounced off indie hit Queen's Domain, try using the cheat code book to give yourself a gun

Queen's Domain's melee combat isn't for everyone: Luckily there's an in-game cheat book you can use to get a gun (and it doesn't bork your achievements cheevos or nothin'). 

First person King's Field/Metroid Prime-like Queen's Domain has quickly become a top-two shortlister for my personal game of the year , but it can be a prickly, difficult-to-recommend game, particularly in its first 30 minutes or so before you get the game-defining Endu airdash sword.

I'm of a mind with news writer Josh Wolens that the contrast between pre- and post-Endu gameplay really helps sell the game's power curve, but our coworkers Andy Chalk and Morgan Park both bounced off Queen's Domain's admittedly sluggish melee combat.

There isn't a difficulty selection in Queen's Domain, but there is something close to it: A "witch's grimoire" where you can input codes to receive unique items. Most of these are references to streamers, content creators, or other indie developers.

While referential, they mesh surprisingly well with Queen's Domain's aesthetic, and I don't think they threaten its overall very deliberate sense of progression. What's more, I say playing the game at all is better than avoiding this little cheat code book out of principle. 

You can enter the code "hempie" (a reference to the vtuber of the same name ) to receive a Soviet SVT-40 semi-automatic battle rifle. A bit incongruous for the medieval fantasy setting, perhaps, but I think it makes for an early game boon while not completely upending Queen's Domain's balance. GTA 6 officially launched worldwide on November 19. However, oodles of players were already going on virtual crime sprees in Leonida well before then thanks to ‘ the New Zealand trick ,’ which allowed them to access the game in the early morning hours of November 18 by switching their consoles to the region.

In just 26 hours, Rockstar’s latest Grand Theft Auto installment has already broken records, becoming the most popular game in both Twitch and Kick history with a combined 1.28 million hours of total broadcast time.

This statistic comes from two separate reports created by Streamlabs and Streamscharts, platforms that aggregate streaming data across the net’s top broadcasting services. Both platforms confirmed that GTA 6 has already enjoyed more than 118 million hours watched as of November 19, with Streamlabs noting this number is 9.7 times greater than hours watched on Just Chatting (12.2 million hours), Twitch’s next most-watched streaming category and a catch-all for broadcasters doing most activities that aren’t strictly gaming.

Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats . But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:

You can't unlock cheats until you've completed the main story. Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

You have to unlock cheats individually through milestones and challenges Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Tarantino’s screenplay, with its novelistic structure and signature oh-so-cool dialogue, is what gives The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth its distinctive rhythm and vibe. Fincher’s exquisite filmmaking eye is still evident throughout, but Cliff Booth is the director’s least emotionally grueling film to date, bereft of the obsessiveness and psychological darkness that’s long been a hallmark of his work. And while Cliff Booth may be David Fincher’s most fun (and funniest) movie, its leisurely pacing and abrupt conclusion may still leave viewers divided.

Taking place over the course of several days in June 1977, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth finds Brad Pitt’s former stuntman now scraping by as a bartender and also a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema , an iconic LA theater that Tarantino has owned for the past couple of decades . Enough people to fill a third of New Zealand’s population changed their console settings to play GTA 6 a day early. Dubbed the “ New Zealand trick ,” the exploit saw players change their region to appear as if they were in another country where the clock struck midnight earliest. 

This happens fairly often for games with a local midnight launch, but GTA 6 saw an unprecedented number of people pretending to be Kiwis. 2 million U.S. and U.K. players took a little trip to New Zealand on November 18 on Xbox alone, according to Ampere Analysis. 

1.5m Xbox users in the U.S. took advantage of the loophole, and 600,000 U.K. Xbox users jumped right in with them. The data also only shows some of the story. Playing early is as easy as changing a setting on Xbox, but PlayStation players have to create a whole new account based in the country, and import PSN currency to spend on the store. 

These frustrating hoops mean the number was likely significantly lower on PS5, but it probably still wasn’t an insignificant number of people considering GTA 6 game sales are expected to lean heavily towards Sony’s platform. So, the total number of fans using the New Zealand trick will be higher.

items.title: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced 'outperformed expectations,' lays off 166 more people anyway

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

Founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched , and underperformance among big releases. Ubisoft said in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced , but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. items.title: Madden Review
items.summary:
Madden is now streaming on Prime Video. 

David O. Russell’s erratically directed Madden is an assemblage of montages in search of a story. Is Madden about the relationship between Oakland Raiders coach John Madden and team owner Al Davis? Is it about John’s struggles to be a husband and father when football’s no longer consuming his life? Is it about John proving himself as an announcer? Is it about the creation of EA’s Madden video game franchise ? 

Madden the movie casts a wide net around all those topics while never satisfactorily exploring them in any real depth or detail, the whole endeavor playing out like SNL skit after SNL skit without anything ever feeling emotionally genuine. It’s one frantically edited, half-explored sequence set to vintage needledrops after another.

Nicolas Cage is packed into a fat suit and prosthetics as the NFL icon, coming across more like a stage actor starring in Shrek the Musical than a real flesh-and-blood person. Yes, John Madden was an over-the-top figure in real life but the movie and Cage turn him into a cartoon character or the big, bumbling oafish dad in a sitcom. ( Will Ferrell was reportedly up to play Madden before Cage.)

Christian Bale is similarly reduced to makeup and mugging as Al Davis, only occasionally hinting at a real person underneath that greasy, gaudy exterior. Davis’ drive to “just win, baby” certainly fed Madden’s hunger for the game and for victory on the field. Their symbiotic relationship here tries to be the film’s main focus, but the slight story never digs much deeper than the superficial.

items.title: Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6
items.summary:
For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 ( well, some of us ) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already. 

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

James Bentley, Hardware Writer 

(Image credit: Future) I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC. 

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my…

Dig is a gem of a TV show, even if it takes a while to pull it from the ground. The new workplace comedy from Amy Poehler and Mike Schur, who previously worked together on the long-running sitcom Parks and Recreation , takes standard issue office hijinx, moves them to a sun-drenched European locale, and weaves in a propulsive mystery that Agatha Christie would be proud of. 

Poehler stars as Elise, the prickly but loveable site manager of an archaeological dig site in Greece. Elise spends her days searching for buried antiquities, wrangling a cadre of horny, fumbling students, and keeping tabs on her pompous dinosaur of a boss, played by Hugh Laurie with a sense of comedic melancholy. 

When Elise is passed over for a promotion after dig leader Neville (Laurie) decides to stick around for another year, she promptly stumbles upon a one-of-a-kind buried artifact and draws a group of colleagues into a web of secrets and mysteries. It’s a shame it takes a while for the show to get rolling because, once it does, it’s thrilling and hilarious.

items.title: As a PC gamer, of course the first thing I did in GTA 6 was try a mouse and keyboard
items.summary:
I am nothing if not entirely predictable. I've waited 13 years to play a new Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6 —and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see. 

GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well.

It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw.

So, I was hoping—hoping against hope, really—that I could just do the same with GTA 6. I was hoping that I could just plug in my little Mountain keyboard and my DeathAdder mouse, and it would just work.

Sadly no, there is no mouse and keyboard support for GTA 6. There is for Xbox, and my keyboard works fine just in the home screens, but as soon as you hit the game itself… nada. Keyboard and mouse support is still very much an occasional thing for Microsoft's console. It is supported, but it's on a per-game basis where devs have to actively code support into their Xbox versions of a title in order for a keyboard and mouse to work. 

It's not actually that rare—some 450 games, and big games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Alan Wake 2, have some level of support for one or both…
items.t: As a PC gamer, of course the first thing I did in GTA 6 was try a mouse and keyboard

I'm not quite sure what to make of this so I'm going to just put it out there: A new Fallout game might soon be headed our way, and it's a hidden object game.

A Wasteland Full of Cats, as it's known, recently appeared on the Australian Classification Board website (via the Fallout subreddit ), and the title pretty much says it all. From the rating:

This game is a hidden object game and the objects you need to find are cats. You play as one of the cats in the Vault. One day there is an accident in the Vault and all of the cats who live there escape out into the Wasteland. It is up to you with the help of some NPCs you meet along the way to find them and return them to the Vault. items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

items.summary:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .

items.summary: It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.
items.t: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices
